content.comment_body: Can someone help me understand why my diagram isn't working as expected? I'm using the left/right cursor keys to cycle through 4 different displays. While this works during simulation, after uploading to [product_name], the cursor keys fail to cycle the displays.
If you programmed the cursor keys as a functional element, you need to also press the ESC key. First, press and hold the ESC key, then press the cursor key.

Glad to hear that it works. Is there a reason a long pause is needed between key presses? For example, pressing ESC+Right, lifting your fingers, then pressing ESC+Right again doesn't work. If you wait a moment before doing ESC+Right again, it does work.

Only [company_name] could fully explain this behavior. In the original [product_name] [article_no] from the first generation, this issue did not exist. I'm unsure about the second generation, but with the current third generation [product_name] [article_no], this is unfortunately the case and cannot be changed.

It's not working consistently. When using the web interface, pages 2, 3, and 4 just display a blank screen while cycling. The model is [article_no] with firmware [version_no]. There might be an issue in the code that needs to be checked. It works fine in simulation, though.
Have you enabled the relevant checkboxes for the webserver in the message texts?
Please refer to the attached file.

Instead of cycling displays individually, you could show all messages simultaneously. Apply high potential to all EN inputs or invert any unconnected EN inputs. This allows scrolling using only the up/down keys, without the ESC key. You can use priority settings to organize the messages as you prefer.
I missed that configuration step, which is why messages weren't displayed via the webserver. Thank you.
Thanks for the suggestion. I'll try that approach.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter inconsistent operation when using cursor keys to cycle displays on [product_name] hardware versus simulation, requiring specific key combinations with delays and encountering blank screens when using the web server. Differences between simulated and real hardware behavior, combined with overlooked web configuration, cause confusion and reduce usability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the display cycling function to behave the same way on both simulation and physical [product_name] hardware, with seamless transitions and reliable operation through the web server interface.
